A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LENSLLM research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, allowing retained, revised and added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning, loss-prediction and model-selection experiments on FLAN, Wikitext and Gigaword, including Figures 3–4 and Tables 2–4.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds original sensitivity experiments in Section 4.4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the output score from r = -exp(ψ(log|D|)) to r = exp(ψ(log|D|)), while retaining selection of the largest r. This localized but consequential edit reverses the stated preference over predicted losses. The NTK scaling model, dataset-halving procedure and stopping logic otherwise remain unchanged; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: The three benchmark datasets remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 adds FLAN scenarios with altered input-length distributions, comparing averages of 18 and 22 tokens against an average of 20; these introduce limited new input conditions.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds Rectified Scaling Law, labeled Rectified, to the efficiency comparison previously containing LENSLLM, SubTuning and FullTuning. The comparator sets in Tables 2 and 3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments sweep regression thresholds 3–5, stopping thresholds 1–5, four learning rates from 3e-5 to 1e-3, and batch sizes 64, 128 and 256. Appendix C.2 also introduces length-based filtering. These extend the evaluation protocol; the original sampling schedule, metrics and benchmark model set remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands robustness analysis: Section 4.4 tests sensitivity to both stopping parameters, Appendix C.1 tests learning-rate and batch-size sensitivity, and Appendix C.2 tests input-length shifts. The corresponding analyses and Tables 5–11 are absent from v1, including its appendices.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains the same RMSE bands. Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests, and the new sensitivity tables provide point estimates without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The result set expands substantially through the sensitivity studies and the added Rectified efficiency curve. Table 2 also changes its multiplier from 10^-2 to 10^-1 with unchanged cell entries: Wikitext OPT-6.7B LENSLLM/Rectified RMSE changes from 0.0026/0.0132 to 0.026/0.132. This revises reported absolute errors tenfold without changing their relative ordering. Tables 3 and 4 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The PAC-Bayesian assumptions, theorems, propositions, corollary and proofs in Appendices A and B remain mathematically unchanged. Renaming the Hessian-based bound and expanding its explanation do not introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same theoretical explanation of fine-tuning phases, NTK-based selection framework and accuracy–efficiency benefits. The headline 91.1% relative accuracy, 85.8% Pearson correlation and 88.5% computational savings are retained; the added experiments support rather than redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of practical robustness to stopping thresholds, learning rates and batch sizes. Appendix C.2 acknowledges decreased performance after input-length shifts while interpreting the limited variation as robustness to moderate changes. These qualifications and interpretations are absent from v1.

D1.justification: v3 adds partial implementation documentation: AdamW, weight decay 0.01, an 80GB NVIDIA A100, PyTorch/Hugging Face Transformers, and an explicit log-sum-exp fitting expression. These are newly disclosed details rather than established changes to existing training. The introduction's anonymous code-link target is replaced by the public repository already linked in v1's abstract.

R1.justification: v3 adds two Wang et al. works on long-tail and dynamic non-IID graph generalization, and more explicitly distinguishes its transformer analysis from Ju et al.'s feed-forward-network bound. Most other reference changes concern publication metadata; Lin et al. and Haowei et al. refer to the same Rectified Scaling Law work.

P1.justification: There are targeted prose clarifications, expanded parameter explanations, terminology corrections, updated correspondence details and acknowledgements. Section 4.4 and Appendix C extend the organization, but the main narrative, section order and most existing text are retained.

P2.justification: Experimental presentation expands substantially with new threshold grids, learning-rate/batch-size grids and an input-length comparison in Tables 5–11. Figure 4 gains a curve, legend entry and annotation; Figure 2 corrects its phase labels. Existing experimental displays are also relocated, while Figures 1 and 3 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful robustness evidence, training details and a fuller efficiency comparison. However, Algorithm 1 removes the negative sign from the predicted-loss score while retaining maximization, introducing a contradiction in the central selection rule. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is a typographical error or a procedural change. The documentation gains and this consequential new inconsistency prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
